title: Manifolds with Boundary Collars and Orientations

items.title: Euclidean upper half-space and its boundary
items.strategy: For n at least one define H^n by x^n at least zero and its coordinate boundary by x^n equals zero; set H^0=R^0 and its boundary empty, so no x^0 occurs.

items.title: Smooth functions on relatively open half-space sets
items.strategy: Use local extension to a smooth function on a Euclidean open neighbourhood; record that this is a local condition on the relative domain.

items.title: Half-space extensions have the same derivatives on the half-space
items.strategy: For two equal extensions, compare derivatives on the dense interior and pass to every boundary point by continuity of Euclidean derivatives.

items.title: Chain rule for smooth half-space maps
items.strategy: Choose local Euclidean extensions, apply the Euclidean chain rule, and use extension-independence before restricting back to the half-space.

items.title: Topological manifolds with boundary
items.strategy: Require Hausdorffness, second countability, and local homeomorphisms to relatively open subsets of H^n; retain dimension zero as a legitimate case.

items.title: Smooth charts, atlases, and structures with boundary
items.strategy: Define compatibility through half-space extension smoothness and define the maximal atlas as all compatible charts, so its construction is not asserted without a criterion.

items.title: Smooth maps between manifolds with boundary
items.strategy: Require every local coordinate representative between relatively open half-space sets to be smooth in the extension sense.

items.title: Boundary smoothness is independent of charts and extensions
items.strategy: Factor two coordinate representatives by source and target transition maps and use the half-space chain rule and derivative-extension lemma.

items.title: Interior and boundary of a manifold with boundary
items.strategy: Initially classify a point by whether a boundary-chart image lies in the coordinate face or in the relative interior, pending the invariance theorem.

items.title: Smooth invariance of the manifold boundary
items.strategy: Extend a transition map and its inverse near a boundary point; their differentials are inverse by the one-sided chain rule. A nonnegative last coordinate of the inverse with an interior zero has zero differential, contradicting invertibility.

items.title: Diffeomorphisms preserve interior and boundary
items.strategy: Apply boundary invariance to coordinate representatives of a diffeomorphism and its inverse.

items.title: The interior is an open smooth n-manifold
items.strategy: Restrict every boundary chart to the coordinate interior and use boundary invariance to make these charts cover precisely the intrinsic interior.

items.title: The boundary of a positive-dimensional manifold is a closed embedded smooth (n-1)-manifold
items.strategy: For n at least one, restrict boundary charts to the face x^n=0, verify transition smoothness by extensions, and read the ambient half-slice to prove closed embeddedness. For n=0 the boundary is empty by convention, so no negative-dimensional manifold is asserted.

items.title: Empty boundary is equivalent to being boundaryless
items.strategy: Use the chart definitions in both directions, with the empty-boundary condition removing all face-chart points.

items.title: Smooth partitions of unity exist on manifolds with boundary
items.strategy: Restrict Euclidean bumps to half-space charts and repeat the countable locally finite shrinking and normalization argument; retain DG-2's AC_omega-sufficient bound.

items.title: Tangent and cotangent bundles extend over a boundary
items.strategy: Define tangent vectors by derivations of boundary germs, identify the coordinate derivation basis by extension-independence, and construct the usual tangent and cotangent transition bundles.

items.title: Inward, outward, and boundary-tangent vectors
items.strategy: Use the sign of the last coordinate in an upper-half-space chart and prove transition invariance from the boundary-preservation differential argument.

items.title: The boundary tangent space is the boundary-tangent hyperplane
items.strategy: Differentiate the restricted face charts and identify their coordinate span with the last-coordinate-zero hyperplane in T_pM.

items.title: Boundary-defining functions
items.strategy: Define a local smooth rho with rho nonnegative, boundary equal to rho^{-1}(0), and nonzero differential on the boundary.

items.title: Boundary-defining functions exist locally and detect inward vectors
items.strategy: Take the last upper-half-space coordinate in a boundary chart and compare any defining function with it; positivity of d rho is exactly the adopted inward sign.

items.title: A global inward-pointing boundary vector field exists
items.strategy: Use an AC_omega-supported boundary-smooth partition to combine local inward coordinate fields after extending each partition-weighted field by zero; convexity preserves strict inwardness.

items.title: Boundary-tangent fields have boundary-preserving local two-sided flows
items.strategy: Restrict the field to the closed embedded boundary, use uniqueness of integral curves, and compare with the ambient local flow.

items.title: Inward-pointing fields have local forward semiflows at the boundary
items.strategy: In a boundary chart extend the field across the face, use Euclidean local flow and the positive normal component to retain nonnegative last coordinate for sufficiently small forward time; make no two-sided-in-M claim.

items.title: Smooth collars of a manifold boundary
items.strategy: Define a collar as an embedding c:partial M times [0,epsilon) to M fixing the boundary at time zero and with image open near the boundary; allow variable widths before shrinking.

items.title: Collar neighborhood theorem
items.strategy: Under AC_omega, flow a global inward field from the boundary. The Euclidean inverse theorem gives local collars; a locally finite positive time function shrinks and patches them on a noncompact boundary, avoiding an unjustified uniform width.

items.title: The double of a smooth manifold with boundary
items.strategy: Glue two labelled copies of M along the identity on their common boundary, retaining the labels so later seam and orientation statements are unambiguous.

items.title: The double has a well-defined smooth structure
items.strategy: Construct the fixed-collar seam atlas and verify quotient topology; interpolate inward vector fields to obtain collar germs, then extend their generator with a proper-exhaustion cutoff and double the resulting boundary-fixing diffeomorphism.

items.title: Smooth functions and tensor fields extend locally across the boundary
items.strategy: Use the double's seam charts to extend across the boundary and restrict back, explicitly denying any canonical choice of extension.

items.title: Immersions and embeddings for manifolds with boundary
items.strategy: Use injectivity of the full tangent differential and homeomorphism onto the image; do not impose neatness, properness, closed image, or boundary-to-boundary behavior.

items.title: Embedded smooth submanifolds with boundary
items.strategy: Define a subset equipped with a boundary-manifold smooth structure whose inclusion is an embedding, without identifying its boundary with its intersection with the ambient boundary.

items.title: Boundary submanifolds of a boundaryless manifold have half-slice charts
items.strategy: Print a boundary constant-rank argument: ordinary slice charts hold at interior points, while a boundary point has the half-slice x^{k+1}=...=x^n=0 with x^k nonnegative.

items.title: Neat submanifolds of a manifold with boundary
items.strategy: Require an embedded boundary submanifold, S intersect boundary M equals boundary S, and transversality to boundary M; neither properness nor closedness is folded into the term.

items.title: Neat submanifolds have boundary-adapted slice charts
items.strategy: Use transversality to straighten boundary M and S simultaneously in half-space coordinates, then identify the induced S boundary with S intersect boundary M.

items.title: Morse-Sard for maps from manifolds with boundary
items.strategy: Apply Morse-Sard separately to the interior and to the (m-1)-manifold boundary, then use a countable-chart null-set union; regular values for both restrictions are dense.

items.title: Determinant-line orientations of finite-dimensional real vector spaces
items.strategy: Refine the published positive-basis-class convention by defining an orientation as a positive ray in det V. The notions agree in positive dimension; this deliberately supplies two signed orientations in dimension zero.

items.title: Orientations and positive basis classes agree in positive dimension
items.strategy: Identify determinant rays with positive-determinant basis classes for n positive; separately note that the unique empty basis sees only the positive zero-dimensional orientation.

items.title: Oriented smooth manifolds and oriented charts
items.strategy: Define a smoothly varying determinant-line ray. For positive dimension use positive coordinate frames; for dimension zero record a sign at each open point instead of pretending the empty frame encodes both choices.

items.title: Positive oriented atlases characterize orientations in positive dimension
items.strategy: Transport determinant rays through charts and use the sign-continuity of nonzero determinants; make the pointwise-sign dimension-zero exception explicit.

items.title: Orientable manifolds
items.strategy: Define orientability as existence of an orientation, not as a hidden simultaneous choice of orientations on arbitrary components.

items.title: Orientability is equivalent to a nowhere-vanishing top form
items.strategy: A top form supplies positive determinant rays; conversely glue local positive top forms with a boundary-smooth partition so the positive weighted sum never vanishes.

items.title: Nonempty connected orientable manifolds have exactly two orientations
items.strategy: Compare two orientations by their locally constant sign ratio on the nonempty connected base; for disconnected spaces retain componentwise choices.

items.title: Pointwise orientation sign of a local diffeomorphism
items.strategy: Compare the induced determinant-line map with the selected rays; in positive dimension it is the Jacobian sign, and on a nonempty connected source the sign is locally constant and hence constant.

items.title: Product orientations
items.strategy: Use the ordered determinant isomorphism det(V direct-sum W)=det(V) tensor det(W) and tensor positive rays, including negatively oriented zero-dimensional factors.

items.title: Orientation induced on a hypersurface by a coorientation
items.strategy: Adopt normal-first order: a coorienting normal followed by a tangent frame is positive exactly when the tangent frame receives the induced orientation.

items.title: Induced boundary orientation
items.strategy: Fix outward-normal-first as the library convention, using the boundary tangent hyperplane and determinant-line rays in all dimensions.

items.title: Boundary orientation is independent of the outward vector field
items.strategy: Two outward vectors differ by a positive normal coefficient plus a tangent vector; determinant multilinearity removes the tangent term and preserves the ray. Compute the interval signs explicitly.

items.title: Boundary orientation of a product with at most one boundary factor
items.strategy: Use the ordered determinant product convention: partial M times N has product boundary orientation, while M times partial N gains (-1)^m. Stop before the unbuilt corners case.

items.title: An oriented transverse normal bundle orients an embedded submanifold
items.strategy: Use the exact sequence 0 to TS to TM restricted to S to normal S to 0 and determinant-line order to solve for any of ambient, tangent, and normal orientations from the other two.

items.title: Orientation-preserving parametrizations
items.strategy: Define a parametrization as orientation preserving when its differential maps the source orientation ray to the target tangent orientation ray; this is the convention consumed by integration charts.

items.title: A smooth chart can turn a boundary point into an interior point
items.strategy: Refute directly with smooth boundary invariance.

items.title: The tangent space at a boundary point has dimension n-1
items.strategy: Refute by separating the full n-dimensional tangent space of M from the (n-1)-dimensional boundary tangent hyperplane.

items.title: Every boundary vector field has a local two-sided flow inside the manifold
items.strategy: Use an outward field on the half-line, which exits immediately; contrast boundary-tangent and inward forward-flow statements.

items.title: An orientable manifold has a canonical orientation
items.strategy: Refute with the two choices on every nonempty connected orientable manifold.

items.title: Every manifold is orientable
items.strategy: Use the Mobius band as the counterexample: transporting a local determinant-line orientation once around its core reverses the ray. Its boundary circle is independently orientable, but no induced boundary orientation exists until the ambient manifold is oriented.

items.title: Boundary orientation is inward-normal-first
items.strategy: Refute against the adopted outward-normal-first convention and the signed boundary of an oriented interval.

title: Manifolds with Boundary Collars and Orientations — Examples

items.title: The closed half-space as a manifold with boundary
items.strategy: Use its identity half-space chart to identify interior and coordinate-face boundary, tangent spaces, and inward/outward signs.

items.title: The closed ball and its sphere boundary
items.strategy: For n at least one, use the Euclidean implicit function theorem on the regular level |x|^2=1 to construct boundary charts for B^n, then use the defining function 1-|x|^2 to identify its boundary as S^{n-1}.

items.title: A cylinder with oppositely oriented boundary components
items.strategy: Apply outward-normal-first to [0,1] times S^1 and calculate that the two circle components receive opposite orientations.

items.title: The boundary of an oriented interval
items.strategy: Use outward normal first at both endpoints to verify partial[a,b]={b}-{a} as determinant-line signs.

items.title: The standard collar of a closed ball
items.strategy: For n at least one, write the collar of S^{n-1} by radial inward displacement and verify its image is a boundary neighbourhood.

items.title: The double of a disk is a sphere
items.strategy: For n at least one, use two closed hemispheres and the seam collar to identify the labelled double of D^n with S^n.

items.title: The Mobius band is nonorientable although its boundary circle is orientable
items.strategy: Follow a local determinant-line orientation around the twisted band and show that it reverses. Independently orient its one-dimensional boundary circle by a parametrization; explicitly, this is not an orientation induced from the nonorientable ambient band.

items.title: Positive-dimensional real projective space is orientable exactly in odd dimension
items.strategy: For n at least one calculate the orientation sign of the antipodal quotient action on S^n; state RP^0 separately as an orientable point.

items.title: The product orientation on a torus
items.strategy: Tensor the positive orientation rays of two circles and compare with the ordered coordinate basis on S^1 times S^1.

items.title: A submanifold meeting the ambient boundary nonneatly
items.strategy: In the half-plane [0,infinity) times R take the embedded interval {0} times [-1,1]; its intersection with the ambient boundary is the entire interval, not its two-point boundary, so it is not neat.

items.title: An inward field without a negative-time flow in the half-line
items.strategy: On [0,infinity), the positive constant field is inward at zero but its negative-time integral curve exits the manifold.

items.title: Boundary orientation of the unit sphere by the outward normal
items.strategy: For n at least one, compare the radial outward-normal-first boundary orientation of the unit ball with the standard hypersurface orientation of S^{n-1}.
